name: intro-to-cta
description: Tap through the intro gate, end the run by intent, and press the CTA on the end screen.
note: Run it with game_run {routine:'intro-to-cta'}. Steps are the game_input vocabulary (tap/key/keys/drag/hover/wait/invoke) plus {type:'command', name} for an intent the scene registered; `expect` holds the ordinary game_run predicates, ANDed and judged once after the last step. A step's `why` and this `note` are documentation — the runner ignores both — but they are why the routine also reads as a checklist. Note what is NOT here: no step calls a component method directly. Ending the run goes through the `finish` command, because a routine that called the handler would prove the handler works while skipping every wire between the player and it.

steps.why: The tap gate is the gesture under test: it hides the overlay and unlocks browser audio, so it is driven as a real tap rather than by dispatching start-game.

steps.name: finish
steps.why: Reveal the end screen by intent instead of waiting out autoWinAfterSec — the timer is a placeholder every real playable replaces, and 15 s of wall clock in every run is a budget nobody gets back.
Button2D needs a real press; this proves the button is on screen and hittable, not just present in the tree.
